Patched the skill. The question was answered correctly and was already well-covered by the existing "Monthly budget/expenditure tables — summing a calendar year" section (which uses national-defense expenditures as its very example). I added the one genuinely new generalizable wrinkle:

- The "absolute percent change between two years' calendar-month sums" wrapper: sum each year's 12 months separately, then |sum_later − sum_earlier| / sum_earlier × 100, base = earlier year, output WITH a "%" sign (12.34% not 0.1234).
- Clarified that "absolute percent change" still normalizes by the base (it's a percent change), and "absolute" only means report the magnitude.
- Sanity note that a >1000% jump from 1940→1953 defense spending is legitimate (wartime/Korea buildup), not an extraction error.

No memory update needed — the cross-session facts (output format, calendar-vs-fiscal trap, native-millions unit) are already captured. Done.
